instructions: Dice the onion until you have about 1 cup. Mince the garlic. Break the noodle sheets into pieces about 1 inch wide.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a 12 inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the turkey, onion and salt. Cook for 6 to 7 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink is left and the onion is soft. If fat has pooled in the pan, spoon it off.
Push the meat to one side. Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the empty side, then the garlic and Italian seasoning. Stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell them, then stir them into the meat.
Add the whole bag of spinach a handful at a time, stirring until it has wilted, about 2 minutes.
Pour in 2 cups of water and the marinara sauce. Add the noodle pieces and press them under the liquid so they're all covered.
Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to medium. Cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir, scraping the bottom of the pan so nothing sticks. Cover and cook for 10 minutes, until the noodles are tender when you poke one with a fork.
Take the skillet off the heat. Dollop the ricotta over the top and scatter on the mozzarella. Cover for 3 minutes, until the mozzarella is slightly melted.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve in bowls with the Parmesan on top.
method_notes: No page for turkey skillet lasagna has 20 ratings, so this is a fallback lead: Posh Journal's skillet lasagna with ground turkey (5.0 from 17), which browns the turkey and onion, wilts in spinach, simmers broken no-boil noodles in jarred sauce and water, then stirs in ricotta and mozzarella off the heat. Life Is But a Dish adds cottage cheese and Simple and Savory uses fewer noodles and less sauce; neither changes the method. The lead says 6 servings, so this makes 4 generous ones. It runs about 42 minutes, since the noodles need 20 covered minutes.
